run_off_road counts all single-vehicle crashes (CRIS manner of collision 'one motor vehicle'); it is a proxy, not a roadway-departure flag.

night = dark lighted, dark not lighted or dark unknown lighting; wet = wet or standing water.

sections.crash_profile: From {{window_start}} to {{window_end}}, {{total_3y}} crashes occurred at this signalized 3-leg intersection. There were {{ka_3y}} fatal or suspected serious injury crashes and {{kabc_3y}} KABCO injury crashes. Rear-end collisions dominated with {{rear_end_3y}} crashes, followed by run-off-road and left-turn opposing types. Night and wet conditions were present in some crashes. Pedestrian and bicycle counts are not available.
sections.why_flagged: The site is flagged due to a model-estimated fatal or serious injury crash rate of {{fsi_rate}} per mile per year and an annual fatal or serious injury frequency of {{annual_fsi}}. Additional risk factors include high traffic exposure ({{aadt}} vehicles/day), multiple marked crossings, and a concentration of crashes within {{window_start}} to {{window_end}}. The site is ranked {{rank_city_actionable}} among actionable city sites and is included in the High Injury Network.

countermeasures.rationale: Adding retroreflective sheeting to signal backplates is supported by broader evidence for all crash types and severities. The cited CMF does not directly match the dominant rear-end crash subtype and requires engineering review. Cites {{cmf:1410}}.

Modifying change plus clearance intervals to ITE 1985 practice is supported by broader evidence for all crash types and severities. The cited CMF does not directly match rear-end or left-turn opposing crash subtypes and requires engineering review. Cites {{cmf:380}}.

sections.benefit_cost: A numerical benefit could not be computed for either countermeasure. The library lacks audit-approved CMFs, planning-level unit costs, and service life data for these entries, and the severity scope does not match fatal or serious injury crashes.
sections.next_steps: Review site geometry, traffic volumes, and existing signal equipment to confirm prerequisites for retroreflective backplates and clearance interval modifications. Conduct engineering review to assess applicability of broader-evidence CMFs to the dominant crash types. Consider further analysis of rear-end crash patterns and signal timing.
